# bharatpii
<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/adarshds1224-pixel/BharatPII/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/adarshds1224-pixel/BharatPII/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

`bharatpii` detects and structurally validates Indian personal identifiers in
data frames (Aadhaar, PAN, GSTIN, IFSC, UPI VPA, mobile numbers, PIN codes and
Voter ID), estimates k-anonymity re-identification risk, computes a technical
readiness score informed by India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP)
Act, 2023, and anonymises flagged columns.

**Important limits.** A valid result means the value is structurally valid
(format and, where one exists, checksum). It does not prove that an identifier
was issued or belongs to anyone. The DPDP Act, 2023 defines "personal data"
(Section 2(t)) and has no statutory category of "sensitive personal data", so
the `risk_tier` labels and the score are package-defined technical conventions.
They are not legal advice or a certification of compliance.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("adarshds1224-pixel/bharatPII")
```

## Example

All data below is synthetic.

```{r example-scan}
library(bharatpii)

set.seed(1)
df <- synthetic_pii(500)

audit <- pii_scan(df)
audit
```

Assess re-identification risk and compute a technical score:

```{r example-score}
quasi <- c("pincode", "dob", "gender")
risk <- reid_risk(df, quasi)
risk

dpdp_score(audit, risk)
```

Anonymise and compare the risk before and after:

```{r example-anonymize}
res <- anonymize(
  df,
  method = c(aadhaar_no = "mask", pan_no = "hash",
             dob = "generalize", pincode = "generalize"),
  salt = "demo-salt-not-for-production",
  quasi_vars = quasi,
  reference_date = as.Date("2024-06-01")
)
res
```
Create a shareable HTML audit report. It is written to a temporary folder
unless you give `output_dir`:

```{r example-report}
path <- report(audit, reid = risk, score = dpdp_score(audit, risk))
path
```

## Features

* Eight identifier detectors with checksum or structure checks (Verhoeff for
  Aadhaar, base-36 for GSTIN).
* `pii_scan()` and `classify_dpdp()` for column-level audits.
* `reid_risk()` for k-anonymity risk, `dpdp_score()` for a 0-100 score.
* `anonymize()`: masking, salted SHA-256 hashing and generalisation.
* `synthetic_pii()`: checksum-valid synthetic data, so no real identifiers are
  ever needed for testing.
* `report()`: an HTML technical audit report (see `?report`).

## Ethics

No real Aadhaar, PAN or other identifiers are used in this package. Test data
is generated by running the checksum algorithms in reverse.
